body:
Makes the net-zero transport correction work on immersed boundary grids and reusable by downstream models. NumericalEarth/Breeze.jl#1209 can then call it instead of carrying its own copy. Bumps the version to 0.117.1.

**Immersed boundaries.** The transport integrals skipped immersed faces, but the correction shifted every face of the boundary plane, which pushed flow through the terrain. For example, with the lower half of an open west boundary immersed, those faces ended up at `u = 0.335` and the net transport seen by the pressure solver was `0.167`. The shifts now skip immersed faces, which stay at exactly zero, and the net transport is at round-off.

**Balanced-transport boundaries.** An imposed `NormalFlowBoundaryCondition(value)` is still never adjusted. A new `BalancedTransport()` scheme lets the correction adjust the imposed value:

```julia
west = NormalFlowBoundaryCondition(U_west; scheme = BalancedTransport())
```

**API.** `enforce_net_zero_transport!` moves from `Models.NonhydrostaticModels` to `Models`. It is exported there alongside `initialize_boundary_transport`. Both accept momentum fields `(; ρu, ρv, ρw)`, in which case the shift is uniform in mass flux.

**Refill.** A halo fill after the correction would revert it. This does not happen in `NonhydrostaticModel`, because `update_state!` fills with `fill_normal_flow_bcs = false`. That was checked over several steps with RK3 and QAB2.

**Tests** (`test/time_stepping/boundary_conditions.jl`):
- immersed faces stay zero and net transport vanishes, with and without the mask;
- `BalancedTransport` inflow and outflow balance under RK3 and QAB2;
- momentum fields with `ρ(z)`.

**Docs.** A short section in `models/boundary_conditions.md`.

title: Net-zero transport: skip immersed faces, opt-in for imposed boundaries, move into Models

body:
This PR bundles three independent distributed-communication fixes for running on GPUs with an MPI that is not CUDA-aware (such as the default `MPICH_jll` binaries) and with NCCL. The diff is +179/−28, about half tests; it can be split into three PRs if reviewers prefer.

## 1. Host-staged communication when MPI is not CUDA-aware

**Symptom.** `Distributed(GPU())` segfaults on the first halo fill (`MPI_Isend`), the first distributed reduction (`MPI_Allreduce`), and distributed FFT transposes (`Alltoall(v)`): device pointers reach an MPI that cannot read them.

**Change.**
- `communication_buffer_array(arch, FT, dims...)` allocates the halo and `TransposableField` buffers. With staging it returns page-locked host memory mapped into the device address space (`CuArray{FT, N, CUDA.HostMemory}`), so pack/unpack kernels work in place and MPI gets a host pointer.
- `all_reduce` and `all_reduce!` copy device arrays through the host when staging.
- Staging is on when `MPI.has_cuda()` is false, can be set with `OCEANANIGANS_HOST_STAGED_COMMUNICATION=true/false`, and never applies to `NCCLDistributed`. **Default behavior changes only where it used to crash.**

**Cost.** Staged exchanges are correct but latency-bound: Breeze's 1680×1680×40 supercell gives 882 / 924 / 830 ms/step on 1/2/4 H100s, against 882 / 480 / 306 with NCCL. Staging makes runs possible without a CUDA-aware MPI; it does not replace one.

## 2. NCCL: corner halos swapped when two ranks share an axis

**Symptom.** With `NCCLDistributed` on 2×2, results differ from serial after one step (2×10⁻⁴ relative in ρv; 2–4% in momentum after 100 steps). 1-D partitions and MPI are exact.

**Cause.** NCCL pairs sends and receives by post order per peer, not by tag. `fill_corners!` posted sends and receives both in SW, SE, NW, NE order, so when corners share a peer each halo receives the peer's same-named corner instead of the opposite one. #5859 fixed this for west/east only; #6449 keeps the old corner order.

**Change.** Send SW, SE, NW, NE and receive NE, NW, SE, SW, so the k-th send from any peer pairs with the right receive. The existing test missed this because it fills each rank with a constant, and on 2×2 all corner neighbors are the same rank; the new test uses a unique function of global (i, j).

## 3. Transposes on a sub-communicator

**Symptom.** A `Distributed` grid on a sub-communicator cannot build a distributed FFT solver (`twin_grid` throws `Partition(2, 1, 1) [2 ranks] inconsistent with 4 MPI ranks`); with equal sizes it would silently mix ranks of different grids.

**Change.** `TransposableField` splits `arch.communicator` instead of `MPI.COMM_WORLD`, and `twin_grid` passes the communicator and devices to its architecture.

## Tests

New `test/mpi/distributed_communication.jl` (4 ranks, `distributed` group): position-dependent halos (edges and corners) and reductions on 4×1, 1×4 and 2×2, with staging off and, on GPU, on; transposes on two disjoint 2-rank sub-communicators (errors on `main`). `test/mpi/nccl.jl` gains a position-dependent corner test.

#6385 (distributed `mean`/`Average`), also needed by NumericalEarth/Breeze.jl#1157, is already merged.

title: Distributed GPU runs without CUDA-aware MPI, NCCL 2-D corner halo fix, transposes on sub-communicators

body:
This PR adds a penetrative radiation correction to the convecting path of CATKE. In practice the convective velocity scale $w_\bigstar$ should depend on the external bouyancy forcing which, with penetrative radiation, is not constrained only on the surface but penetrates inside the mixed layer. Therefore, we should account for the integral of this forcing within the mixed layer. We also need to compute the convective length scale, which in CATKE is a measure of the mixed layer depth, and in the case of penetrative radiation requires an inversion to compute. Here it is implemented with 3 Newton iterations which (claude) verified is enough for any practical case.

To be more detailed, in a convection event, CATKE need a measure of $w_\bigstar$ and a measure of the convective mixing length. The latter is just an estimate of the mixed layer so I will call it $h$.
As per [Wagner et al 2025](https://agupubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1029/2024MS004522), the assumed relation is
```math
w_\bigstar^3 \sim  h J^b
```
which comes from the assumption that the turbulent flux $w^\prime b^\prime$ is linear inside the mixed layer ($b$ is uniform) and $J^b$ is the (positive) buoyancy flux at the surface.

Now, if we introduce radiation, the balance above changes Let's start with the buoyancy budget
```math
\partial_t b = -\partial_z F = -\partial_z (\overline{w'b'} + F^r )
```
where
```math
\overline{w'b'}(0) = J^{bc}, \qquad F(0) = J^{bc} + J^r = J^b .
```
Note that $J^r$ is always negative as the solar radiation is the only penetrating radiation and $|J^{bc}| > |J^r|$ with $J^{bc}$ positive since we are in a convecting regime (solar radiation at the surface reduces convection).

Again, we assume that (1) the layer is well mixed ($b$ is uniform in $-h < z < 0$) then $F$ should be linear in $z$, and (2) there is no entrainment at the bottom of the mixed layer (same assumption of base CATKE) which means that $\overline{w'b'}(-h) = 0$ and the flux at the bottom of the mixed layer is just the penetrating radiation
```math
F(-h) = J^r \mathcal{T}(- h)
```
where $\mathcal{T}$ is the trasmitted fraction of the (surface) penetrating radiation $J^r$.
Then a linear $F$ is easily computed as 
```math
F(z) = J^b + (J^b - J^r \mathcal{T}(- h)) \frac{z}{h}
```
and the turbulent flux is therefore
```math
\overline{w'b'}(z) = F(z) - F^r(z) = J^b + (J^b - J^r \mathcal{T}(-h)) \frac{z}{h} - J^r \mathcal{T}(- z)
```
We then integrate in the layer the turbulent flux to get
```math
\int_{-h}^0 \overline{w'b'} dz = w_\bigstar = \frac{h}{2}(J^b + J^r \mathcal{T}(-h)) - J^r \int_{-h}^0 \mathcal{T} dz
```
we normalize by 2 to keep the same scaling of the original CATKE implementation with no radiation.

In the limit of radiation absorbed at the surface $\mathcal{T}(-h) = 0$ and $\int_{-h}^0\mathcal{T}dz = 0$ returns back the previous formulation and in the limit of radiation passing through ($\mathcal{T}(h) = 1$ and $\int_{-h}^0 \mathcal{T} dz = h$) we recover $w_\bigstar^3 = h(J^b - J^r) = hJ^{bc}$ meaning that radiation is not accounted for in the mixed layer buoyancy budget at all.

Now, this formulation is a bit more complicated and requires a newton solve to find $h$ which is out convective mixing length. cc @rafferrari 

@glwagner I would need your expertise here to understand if this implementation is sensible or not.
title: Penetrative radiation interface in `Forcings` and practical application in CATKE

body:
This fixes a compilation failure which appeared in #5799, because `_compute_tripolar_coordinates!` is now type-unstable.  PR easier to review by [ignoring whitespace changes](https://github.com/CliMA/Oceananigans.jl/pull/6467/changes?w=1).

> `_compute_tripolar_coordinates!` looped over `zip`ped tuples of the four coordinate arrays per location. `StaticStridesOffsetArray` carries the array size in its type, and with a face-located fold pivot the arrays at y-faces have one more row than those at y-centers, so these tuples are heterogeneous. Julia does not unroll a `for` loop over a tuple, so each element was fetched with a dynamic `getfield` and the loop body was type-unstable. That is only slow when the kernel runs as plain Julia on the host, but the kernel cannot be compiled for GPU-like backends, where the dynamic tuple indexing is invalid IR.
>
> Move the loop body into an `@inline` function and call it once per location, so every call is type-stable.
title: Compute tripolar coordinates with one call per location

A `Field` allocated inside a Reactant-compiled function has a `TracedRNumber` element type. Indexing it, for example `column[1, 1, k]` on a `Field{Nothing, Nothing, Center}`, throws a `MethodError` because two methods are equally specific:

```
getindex(r::Field{Nothing, Nothing}, i, j, k)                                    @ Oceananigans.Fields field.jl
getindex(a::AbstractArray{TracedRNumber{T}, N}, index::Vararg{Union{Int64, TracedRNumber{Int64}}, N})  @ Reactant.TracedIndexing
```

The Oceananigans methods specialize on the location but take untyped indices, while Reactant's specialize on the indices. This PR adds `getindex` and `setindex!` methods to `OceananigansReactantExt` for every combination of reduced and unreduced dimensions. Each method is more specific than both and drops the index along reduced dimensions, as the methods in `src/Fields/field.jl` do.

Found in Breeze (NumericalEarth/Breeze.jl#1188), which currently works around it by indexing `field.data`.

**Test.** A new testset in `test/reactant/unit.jl` indexes and assigns into a full field and a column field allocated inside a compiled function. It fails with the ambiguity on `main` and passes with this change (checked locally on CPU with the test environment's Reactant 0.2.299). I did not run the full Reactant suite.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
title: Index fields with a traced element type without ambiguity

## Purpose 

Reactant integration currently defines too specialized `traced_type_inner` methods that make `@nospecialize` and `@nospecializeinfer` non functional on those methods.

This PR correctly despecializes `traced_type_inner` methods, as discussed in https://github.com/CliMA/Oceananigans.jl/pull/6375#pullrequestreview-5696829465

## To-do

## Content

the following code
```julia
@nospecialize(T::Type{Oceananigans.AbstractOperations.ConditionalOperation{LX, LY, LZ, F, C, O, G, M}}),
```
has no effect because `T` is a fully specificed concrete type, but `@nospecialize` (and `@nospecializeinfer`) take effect on partially specified types (e.g. `AbstractArrays`, `Union`, `UnionAll`, ...).

Then gain is small overall, but reduces TTFX of `traced_type` by 40-50%.

A `KernelFunctionOperation` built inside a traced function and passed to a kernel inside a `NamedTuple` fails under Reactant:

```
MethodError: Cannot `convert` an object of type
  KernelFunctionOperation{…, LatitudeLongitudeGrid{CuTracedRNumber{Float64,1}, …}, Float64, …}
to an object of type
  KernelFunctionOperation{…, LatitudeLongitudeGrid{CuTracedRNumber{Float64,1}, …}, CuTracedRNumber{Float64,1}, …}
```

The two sides disagree about the element type `T`:

* `Adapt.adapt_structure` sets `T = unwrapped_eltype(eltype(κ))`, i.e. `Float64`.
* `Reactant.traced_type_inner` in `OceananigansReactantExt` recomputes `T2 = eltype(G2)` from the traced grid, i.e. `CuTracedRNumber{Float64,1}`.

This PR maps `T` through `traced_type_inner` like the other type parameters, so the traced type agrees with the adapted object.

The failure only appears when the grid's float type is traced (so the operation is built inside `@jit`) *and* the operation is nested in a container. When it is passed bare, or built outside `@jit`, it works. The new test in `test/reactant/unit.jl` covers this case. It fails on `main` and passes here. The existing `KernelFunctionOperation` reduction tests also pass.

Found in NumericalEarth/NumericalEarth.jl#401.

body:
## Problem

`HorizontalScalarBiharmonicDiffusivity` is not dissipative on a `PartialCellBottom` grid. Where a thin partial cell
neighbours a thick one, the operator can increase kinetic energy and its spectral radius grows with the thickness ratio,
so explicit time stepping blows up.

We hit this in a single-level 0.36ᵒ global tide model (`TripolarGrid`, `PartialCellBottom` with true depths and
`minimum_fractional_cell_height = 1e-3`). With a 5 m minimum depth, η reached 6 km within 0.02 days. With a 20 m minimum
depth it went NaN at about day 2. A flat 2D biharmonic applied as a forcing is stable.

## Mechanism

For the horizontal formulation, the stresses are

    τᵤₓ = τᵥᵧ = ν δ★,  τᵤᵧ = -τᵥₓ = -ν ζ★,  with δ★ = div(Q), ζ★ = curl(Q),  Q = (∇²h u, ∇²h v).

Here `div` and `curl` are unweighted 2D operators. The outer divergence `∂ⱼτᵢⱼ` is thickness-weighted:

    ∂ⱼτ₁ⱼ = V⁻¹ᶠᶜᶜ [ δx(Δy Δzᶜᶜᶜ τᵤₓ) + δy(Δx Δzᶠᶠᶜ τᵤᵧ) ],    Vᶠᶜᶜ = Az Δzᶠᶜᶜ.

The inner Laplacian `∇²hᶠᶜᶜ u = V⁻¹ᶠᶜᶜ [δx(Δy Δzᶜᶜᶜ ∂x u) + δy(Δx Δzᶠᶠᶜ ∂y u)]` is weighted the same way. With
`PartialCellBottom`, `Δzᶠᶜᶜ = min(Δzᶜᶜᶜ(i-1), Δzᶜᶜᶜ(i))`. Two things go wrong:

1. **No bound.** The thick cell's stress, `Δy Δz_thick τ`, is divided by the thin face's volume `Az Δz_thin`. Both
   Laplacians gain a factor of `Δz_thick / Δz_thin`, about 800 for 5 m next to 4000 m. The spectral radius of `∇⁴` grows
   by roughly the square of that factor.
2. **Not symmetric.** The outer operator is the vector-invariant Laplacian (`∇ div − curl curl`), while the inner one is
   componentwise. They are adjoint, and their cross terms `∂x(Δz ∂y Qᵥ) − ∂y(Δz ∂x Qᵥ)` cancel, only when Δz is laterally
   uniform. Otherwise `Σ V u·G` is not sign-definite.

## Reproducer

```julia
using Oceananigans, Random, Printf

Nx = Ny = 32; Δ = 10e3; H = 4000; Δt = 600
underlying_grid = RectilinearGrid(size=(Nx, Ny, 1), x=(0, Nx*Δ), y=(0, Ny*Δ), z=(-H, 0), halo=(4, 4, 4),
                                  topology=(Periodic, Periodic, Bounded))
Random.seed!(1234)
bottom = - 5 .- (H - 5) .* rand(Nx, Ny)  # depths between 5 m and 4000 m
grid = ImmersedBoundaryGrid(underlying_grid, PartialCellBottom(bottom; minimum_fractional_cell_height=1e-3))

for g in (underlying_grid, grid)
    model = HydrostaticFreeSurfaceModel(g; closure=HorizontalScalarBiharmonicDiffusivity(ν=Δ^4/1000Δt),
                                        momentum_advection=nothing, tracers=(), buoyancy=nothing,
                                        free_surface=ImplicitFreeSurface())
    set!(model, u=(x, y, z) -> randn(), v=(x, y, z) -> randn())
    for n in 1:2000
        time_step!(model, Δt)
    end
    @printf("%s: max|u| = %.3e\n", nameof(typeof(g)), maximum(abs, model.velocities.u))
end
```

`ν Δt / Δ⁴ = 10⁻³`, far inside the flat-bottom stability limit.

| 32 × 32 × 1, 2000 steps, initial max\|u\| = 4.17 | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| flat bottom | 0.343 | 0.343 (same code path) |
| `PartialCellBottom`, all full cells | 0.343 | 0.343 |
| `PartialCellBottom`, random depths 5–4000 m | blows up at step 2 (max\|u\| = 1.5e5) | 1.12 |
| `PartialCellBottom`, 5 m / 4000 m checkerboard | blows up at step 1 (max\|u\| = 5.1e3) | 0.80 |

The operator check builds the viscous operator `G` as a matrix on an 8 × 8 periodic grid. It then computes the largest
energy growth rate, `max over u of (d/dt ½ΣV|u|²) / (½ΣV|u|²)`, and the spectral radius of `G`, both in units of `ν/Δ⁴`:

| 8 × 8 × 1 | growth rate `main` | growth rate this PR | spectral radius `main` | spectral radius this PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| flat bottom | −1e−14 | −1e−14 | 64 | 64 |
| `PartialCellBottom`, random depths 5–4000 m | **+692** | +7e−15 (round-off) | **22,370** | 40.6 |
| `PartialCellBottom`, random depths and land | **+160** | +8e−15 (round-off) | **4,435** | 32.3 |
| same, `Bounded` in x and y | **+33.7** | −5e−15 (round-off) | **4,242** | 25.1 |

## Fix

On grids with partial cells (`PCBIBG`), `∇⁴` becomes the square of one thickness-weighted vector Laplacian:

    G = −ν L(L(u)),   L(u) = V⁻¹ [ ∇(Az Δz★ div u) − ẑ × ∇(Az Δzᶠᶠᶜ ζ u) ],
    Δz★ᶜᶜᶜ = min(Δzᶠᶜᶜ(i), Δzᶠᶜᶜ(i+1), Δzᶜᶠᶜ(j), Δzᶜᶠᶜ(j+1)).

* The inner Laplacian `Q = L(u)` uses the same div/curl structure and thickness weights as the outer divergence, so
  `L` is symmetric and negative semi-definite in the volume-weighted inner product. Then
  `Σ V u·G = −ν Σ V |L u|² ≤ 0` for any Δz.
* The centre stresses are weighted by `Δz★`, the thinnest adjacent velocity face, instead of `Δzᶜᶜᶜ`. Corner stresses
  already use `Δzᶠᶠᶜ`, which is the minimum of the four cells. Every stress is therefore at most as thick as the faces
  it acts on, so the spectral radius is no larger than for a flat bottom, and the time-step limit does not depend on the
  partial cells. The `Δz★/Δzᶜᶜᶜ` rescaling is applied to `δ★ᶜᶜᶜ`, so the generic flux-form outer divergence
  (`∂ⱼ_τ₁ⱼ`, `∂ⱼ_τ₂ⱼ`) is unchanged and momentum remains a flux divergence of face fluxes.
* Corner (vorticity) stresses are zeroed on all peripheral nodes, walls included, in both `L` and the outer `ζ★`. This
  matches what `conditional_flux_ffc` already does at immersed boundaries. Without it, the operator was still
  non-dissipative next to `Bounded` walls with partial cells (+6.7e−3 ν/Δ⁴).

This is implemented as two methods, `δ★ᶜᶜᶜ(i, j, k, grid::PCBIBG, u, v)` and `ζ★ᶠᶠᶜ(i, j, k, grid::PCBIBG, u, v)`, plus
`@inline` helpers in `abstract_scalar_biharmonic_diffusivity_closure.jl`. It allocates nothing and uses no new halos.
`HorizontalFormulation` is the case fixed and tested here. `HorizontalDivergenceFormulation` also goes through `δ★ᶜᶜᶜ`, so it picks up the bounded weights, but its divergence-only outer operator is not exactly adjoint to the full inner `L` when Δz varies, and this PR does not test its dissipativity.

### What changes and what does not

* **Grids without partial cells** (non-immersed, `GridFittedBottom`, and so on): the code path is untouched, so results
  are bitwise identical.
* **`PartialCellBottom` with uniform Δz on a periodic `RectilinearGrid`**: identical to round-off (≤ 1e−12 relative),
  since the vector-invariant and componentwise Laplacians agree algebraically there. This is tested.
* **`PartialCellBottom` on `Bounded` walls**: the biharmonic corner stress at the walls is now zero (free slip), as it
  already was at immersed boundaries. On a uniform-Δz bounded grid this changes the spectral radius from 59.40 to
  59.22 ν/Δ⁴. Both versions are dissipative.
* **Curvilinear grids** (`LatitudeLongitudeGrid`, tripolar): with partial cells the operator is now the vector-invariant
  form. The flux-form outer divergence (`δx(Δyᶜᶜᶜ …)` rather than `Δyᶠᶜᶜ δx(…)`) is not exactly self-adjoint where
  `Δxᶜᶠᶜ ≠ Δxᶜᶜᶜ`. That is a metric effect that `main` already has on grids without immersed boundaries (growth rate
  ≈ 2e−3 of the spectral radius on an 8 × 8 lat-lon grid, unchanged by this PR). With partial cells and land, this PR
  reduces that ratio from 3.8e−3 to the same 2.0e−3 as without partial cells, and the spectral radius by 125×.

Tracer biharmonic diffusion needs no change. Its inner and outer Laplacians are both `V⁻¹ δ(A ∂c)`, which is symmetric,
and the face areas use the thinner neighbour, so it is bounded.

## Tests

New file `test/turbulence_closures/biharmonic_partial_cells.jl`:

* **Dissipation inequality**: for `PartialCellBottom` over random depths (with and without land, periodic and bounded),
  the largest energy growth rate is ≤ 1e−12 × the spectral radius, and the spectral radius is ≤ the flat-bottom one.
* **Stays bounded**: random velocities over random depths decay over 200 steps, as they do over a flat bottom.
* **Uniform Δz**: tendencies on a `PartialCellBottom(-H)` grid match the grid without partial cells to 1e−12.

On `main`, the first two fail (growth rate +692 ν/Δ⁴; the model blows up at step 2).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
title: Make horizontal biharmonic viscosity dissipative on PartialCellBottom grids

title: Bump Enzyme in /docs

body:
Main's Reactant unit tests fail since 66207970 with

```
UndefVarError: `T` not defined in `OceananigansReactantExt`
  traced_type_inner(OA::Type{<:KernelFunctionOperation}, ...) at ext/OceananigansReactantExt/OceananigansReactantExt.jl:121
```

#6468 despecialized `traced_type_inner` for `KernelFunctionOperation`, reading the parameters from `OA.parameters` and discarding `T` as `_`. #6375, merged 40 minutes later, traces `T` to keep the operation's eltype. Each was fine on its own; together `T` is unbound. This binds it.

Every testset that reduces or passes a `KernelFunctionOperation` under tracing fails on main for this reason ("KernelFunctionOperation reductions on LatitudeLongitudeGrid", "… on RectilinearGrid", "… as a kernel argument", "Computed fields on a grid with an array-valued vertical coordinate", "Reductions of AbstractOperations"), and every open PR that merges main inherits it.
